tip: The '-yle' on 'aceleyle' turns the noun 'acele' (haste) into an adverb: with haste, hurriedly.
'yürüyerek' adds '-yerek' to 'yürü' (walk) to mean 'by walking'; '-erek' shows the manner of an action.
'doğru' means 'toward' and follows the '-a' form: 'akşam' takes '-a', giving 'akşama doğru' = toward evening.
'yerine' = 'instead of' and needs the '-in' (of) ending: 'annem' + '-in' gives 'annemin yerine' = in place of my mother.
The '-ken' ending means 'while': it attaches to 'geçer' (crosses) to give 'geçerken' = while crossing, happening at the same time.
'arabalar' is plural but the verb stays singular: 'bekledi', not 'beklediler'. Non-human plural subjects normally take a singular verb.
'unutmak' takes the '-mayı' form: 'al' (take) + '-mayı' = 'almayı', so 'almayı unuttum' = I forgot to take.
'ailece' adds '-ce' to 'aile' (family) to mean 'as a family, all together'; '-ce' marks doing something collectively.
'gönderir' is the '-ir' form, used for habits: with 'her sabah' it means 'sends every morning', not right now.
'gittiğimde' means 'when I go': 'git' + '-tiğimde'. The '-diğimde' ending marks 'when someone does something'.
'sergileniyor' is passive: 'sergile' (exhibit) + '-n-' = 'is exhibited'. The '-n-' makes the action happen to the subject.
To want someone else to act, use '-masını istemek': 'oyna' + '-masını' = 'oynamasını', with 'çocukların' in the '-ın' (of) form.
'yanında' (next to) needs the '-un' (of) ending on the noun: 'okul' + '-un' = 'okulun yanında' = next to the school.
'kütüphanedeki' adds '-ki' to the '-de' (in) form: 'kütüphanede' (in the library) + '-ki' = 'the ones in the library'.
Here 'geldi' (from 'gelmek', to come) means 'seemed': 'pahalı geldi' = came across as expensive, not literally arrived.
'varmış' adds '-mış' for reported or inferred facts: 'there used to be, apparently'. It marks things you did not witness.
'keşke' pairs with the '-sa' (if) form for a wish: 'olsa' = 'if only there were', so 'keşke ... olsa' = I wish.
'ağaçtan' uses the '-tan' (from) ending: 'ağaç' + '-tan' = from the tree. It marks the source of the action.
'yapabilirim' shows ability with '-abil': 'yap' (do) + '-abil' + '-irim' = 'I can make'. '-abil' means 'be able to'.
'göre' (according to) follows the '-ya' (to) form: 'anlaşma' + '-ya' = 'anlaşmaya göre' = according to the agreement.
'almalıymış' is built on '-malı' = must/should: 'al' + '-malı' = 'should take'. '-malı' expresses necessity.
'yüzünden' = 'because of' and marks a bad cause: 'sıkışıklığı yüzünden' = due to the jam. It is normally used for negative reasons.
'unutmuşum' uses '-muş' in the first person for a realization: 'I've forgotten', softer than the plain 'unuttum'.
After a number the noun stays singular: 'beş ağaç' = five tree(s), never 'beş ağaçlar'. No plural suffix follows a count.
'bulup' uses '-ip' to chain two verbs sharing one subject: 'bul' (find) + '-up', then 'çalıştım' = 'found ... and studied'.
'gelen' turns a verb into an adjective with '-en': 'gel' (come) + '-en' = 'who come', describing 'misafirlere' (the guests).
'etmişti' is the 'had done' form ('-mişti'): the tackle happened before he was sent off, an earlier past.
Add '-la/-le' to a noun to build a manner adverb. 'heyecan' (excitement) becomes 'heyecanla', meaning with excitement.
The yes/no word 'mu' stands as its own word, harmonizes, and carries the person ending: 'istiyor musun' means do you want.
The '-ma' ending turns a verb into a noun. 'kapanmak' (to close) becomes 'kapanması', the closing of it, with '-sı' marking whose.
